title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - streaming stability, functions, roles, stop/logprobs, formatting
author: Asha Patel
description: This PR brings Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer closer to feature parity for /v1/chat.completions. It implements: role-preserving input/response mapping, stop token handling, logprobs passthrough (when supported by the runtime), improved response formatting for structured outputs and function/tool calling, and a series of streaming stability fixes that reduce jitter and ensure proper chunk boundaries for function call events. Motivation: several customers and internal evals rely on OpenAI-compatible behavior for migration; we need deterministic behavior for roles/stop, and streaming must not split function call JSON across chunks. Changes include runtime patches, API surface adapters, unit/integration tests, and docs updates. Checklist: - [x] Implement role mapping and role validation - [x] Add stop token logic with priority rules matching OpenAI semantics - [x] Wire logprobs through from runtime when available and document fallbacks - [x] Stabilize streaming boundaries for function calls and structured output - [x] Add comprehensive tests (unit + e2e) - [x] Update OpenAI-compat docs and examples Notes: there are minor behavioral differences documented in release notes for edge cases where underlying model does not return logprobs; in those cases we return null to match existing SDK expectations. Internal Linear: ENG-4182 covers API semantics; ENG-4190 covers streaming stability and perf regression verification.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Overall looks good. Two requests: 1) add an explicit doc note about behavior when logprobs are unavailable from the backend, 2) make sure role validation rejects unknown roles earlier to avoid runtime surprises.
Asha Patel (author): Addressed both comments; added doc note and pre-validate roles in chat_completions.py. PTAL.

Jordan Kim: Streaming changes are critical. I saw a flaky failing test in the first CI run caused by an off-by-one when slicing buffers; please add a regression test. Also flagging potential perf impact of additional memcpy in streamer.cpp.
Asha Patel: Added regression test and switched to zero-copy path where possible; perf microbenchmarks show <1% impact on tail latency.
Elena Ruiz: Approved after verifying e2e tests on dedicated infra. Two minor nits inline but not blocking.
merge_commit_message: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - roles, stop/logprobs, streaming stability, and structured output
release_notes:
Enhancements: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: role-preserving mapping, stop token handling, logprobs passthrough when supported, stabilized streaming for function calls and structured outputs. See docs/openai-compat/chat-completions.md for migration notes.
Behavioral note: when the underlying model or runtime cannot produce logprobs, the compatibility layer returns null for logprobs fields to avoid surprising consumers.
